hero.headline: Foundation's content, turned into *pipeline*.
hero.intro: A full breakdown of where Foundation's channels stand today, what I'm proposing to change, why, and exactly how it maps back to the 5 things you asked for. Built to be reviewed, argued with, and edited.

score.label: Channel readiness today
score.headline: 4.3/10 across 7 channels. The plan targets **8.0** by day 90.

summary.title: Where *Foundation* stands today
summary.verdict: The cadence is strong and the voice is distinctive, but **almost everything runs through Ross**, video is inconsistent, and nothing yet connects content to closed deals. In 90 days: every channel on a repeatable cadence, ABM shipped, and **one closed deal traced back to this plan**.

working.title: Ross shows up constantly
working.detail: More than six or seven LinkedIn posts a week, plus thought leadership ads around events. Cadence is not the problem.

working.title: A distinctive voice on X
working.detail: The account that needs the least repositioning of any channel. When threads land, they land well.

working.title: A warm audience already exists
working.detail: 100K podcast listeners. YouTube isn't a cold start.

working.title: Exit Five already trusts Ross
working.detail: Dave Gerhardt has publicly vouched for him. The job is to compound that relationship, not build one from zero.

notDoing.title: Activating the VP team
notDoing.detail: Ross is the only one posting regularly. More credible voices mean more touchpoints with buyers.

notDoing.title: LinkedIn-native, long-form thinking
notDoing.detail: Much of the content is repurposed or pre-written short form, and can feel formulaic enough to scroll past.

notDoing.title: Publishing video consistently
notDoing.detail: Uploads are too irregular to build repeat viewers, and one channel is trying to serve two audiences.

notDoing.title: Using X threads and articles
notDoing.detail: No regular thread cadence, and no use yet of X's long-form article format.

notDoing.title: Showing up in Exit Five at volume
notDoing.detail: Participation is light-touch rather than constant, public and compounding.

missing.title: One Instagram account with a clear job
missing.detail: @rosssimmondsig and @thecoolestcool split one audience and neither is clearly positioned.

missing.title: A bottom-of-funnel video layer
missing.detail: Nothing tactical and persona-specific to send a prospect three calls into a sales conversation.

missing.title: An ABM program for dream accounts
missing.detail: No personalised, physical outreach to the short list of accounts worth a large deal.

missing.title: Content-to-pipeline attribution
missing.detail: No way to see which posts, issues or touchpoints influenced a closed deal.

missing.title: A physical touchpoint
missing.detail: Every touchpoint competes in the same crowded inbox and feed.

channels.name: LinkedIn
channels.summary: Own Ross's presence around SEO, AEO, GEO, YouTube and content marketing, and activate the full VP leadership team.
audit: **Consistent posting.** Ross is currently the only one posting regularly from both his personal profile and the company page.
**Largely repurposed.** Much of the content feels pre-written or repurposed from other platforms rather than made for LinkedIn.
**Limited thought leadership.** Very little long-form, deep content that establishes Ross as a thought leader.
**VP team underused.** Their profiles could create additional touchpoints with potential customers.
**Too pre-crafted.** Posts can feel formulaic, which makes them easier to scroll past.
**Commercial upside.** A warmed-up audience makes webinars and offers easier to sell, including with paid ads.

plan.title: AEO/GEO frontier takes
plan.detail: Specific, data-backed opinions on where AI search is heading, the format already landing hardest.

plan.title: Foundation client proof
plan.detail: Real, named results (with permission), framed as a story. Can run as ads.

plan.title: Contrarian marketing opinion
plan.detail: A defensible counter-take to conventional wisdom, once a week.

plan.title: Behind the build of Distribution.ai
plan.detail: Founder-journey content watched by exactly the ICP that needs Foundation.

plan.title: Newsletter and podcast repurposing
plan.detail: 'What Matters This Week' and 'Create Like The Greats' cut into standalone posts within 48 hours.

plan.title: Executive track
plan.detail: Biweekly interviews with each of the 6 executives; I write, they approve. Ross at 8-10 posts a week, each VP at 5.

channels.name: X / Twitter
channels.summary: Systemise @TheCoolestCool around the same pillars as LinkedIn, native to how X is actually read. The bio is strong; no change needed.
audit: **Strong, distinctive voice.** Needs more volume of the same kind of content, not repositioning.
**Threads aren't consistent.** When they land (the psychology thread), they land well, but there's no regular cadence.
**No long-form articles.** A real gap given how much long-form thinking already exists in the newsletter.

plan.title: Short tweets
plan.detail: 3-4 a day. Already working; just increase the cadence.

plan.title: Threads
plan.detail: 12-tweet breakdowns of one specific idea, three times a week, from the same source material as the LinkedIn pillars.

plan.title: Long-form
plan.detail: 2 X articles a month, a deeper cut of the strongest newsletter issue.

channels.name: Instagram
channels.summary: Merge @rosssimmondsig and @thecoolestcool into one account positioned as Ross's speaker and author channel. Not built for enterprise lead gen.
audit: **One audience, split in half.** A follower of one account has no reason to know the other exists.
**No clear job.** @thecoolestcool is more active and personal; @rosssimmondsig posts clips. Neither is clearly positioned.
**Not a content gap.** The problem is structure and positioning, not effort.

plan.title: Merge the accounts
plan.detail: One account with a narrow job: keep Ross top of mind with a personal audience, after work hours.

plan.title: Position Ross as a working speaker and author
plan.detail: Pipeline stays with LinkedIn, X and ABM; Instagram keeps him likeable and visible between them.

plan.title: Content split
plan.detail: Stage clips 35%, behind the scenes 30%, casual marketing takes 20%, author content 15%.

channels.name: YouTube
channels.summary: Split into two layers with two jobs: a discovery channel built for volume, and a small, high-value series for buyers close to a decision.
audit: **Strong core asset.** 100K podcast listeners is a real, warm audience.
**Consistency is the gap.** Uploads are too irregular to build habitual, repeat viewers.
**Two audiences, one channel.** Casual podcast discoverers and people wanting tactical walkthroughs dilute each other.

plan.title: Layer 1, TOFU: 4 videos a month
plan.detail: Industry-focused discovery content, built on outlier research before any script is written.

plan.title: Ross's expertise as raw material
plan.detail: Top LinkedIn and blog posts become scripts; AI only structures them for YouTube.

plan.title: One hook and body format
plan.detail: What it's about, why keep watching, why Ross is credible; then a numbered body. CTAs at ~33% and at the end.

plan.title: Layer 2, BOFU: low volume, high value
plan.detail: Real conversations with Foundation's strategists, walking through tactics for a specific persona. Sent to prospects mid-sales-cycle.

plan.title: Judge at 90 days
plan.detail: Expect the first 1-2 leads or demos around the 90-day mark.

channels.name: Exit Five
channels.summary: Not a light-touch presence. The goal is volume with substance, compounding Ross's existing relationship with the community.
audit: **Not a cold community.** Dave Gerhardt has publicly said there's no one better to teach content distribution than Ross.
**The bar is volume.** One polished post a month won't compound the relationship.

plan.title: Weekly participation rhythm
plan.detail: Answering questions and showing up in active threads, not just posting Foundation content.

plan.title: Share every real touchpoint
plan.detail: A person met, a tool built, a campaign run: posted as it happens.

plan.title: Dave Gerhardt collaboration
plan.detail: A specific proposal for a joint session or guest appearance.

plan.title: A pathway to pipeline
plan.detail: Repeat engagers get a warm next step: a resource, the magazine list, or a direct conversation.

plan.title: The magazine's launch channel
plan.detail: Exit Five becomes the go-to-market for the monthly magazine.

channels.name: Magazine
channels.summary: An evolved, physical version of the newsletter: a month of thinking, delivered to one specific person's desk.
audit: **Every digital touchpoint competes** in the same crowded inbox and feed.
**The bet:** while competitors invest harder in digital noise, the most memorable thing Foundation can send is something physical and worth sitting with.

plan.title: Three audiences
plan.detail: Active clients (retention, expansion), warm pipeline prospects, and a small run to dream accounts.

plan.title: Free to start
plan.detail: A relationship asset, not a revenue line. Test paid only once engagement is proven.

plan.title: Issue structure
plan.detail: Flagship long-form piece, client spotlight, contrarian take, monthly digest, one data drop, a guest thought leader, a 'Ross is reading' column.

plan.title: Monthly production
plan.detail: Week 1 content lock, week 2 design, week 3 print and proof, week 4 ship plus a PDF to newsletter subscribers.

channels.name: ABM
channels.summary: Three physical direct-mail campaigns for Foundation's highest-value dream accounts, built with the sales team.
audit: **Everything else here is demand generation:** broad content that lets buyers self-select.
**ABM works backwards:** pick the dream accounts first, then build something personal for each one.
**Cold email** gets around a 1-3% reply rate; a well-built physical ABM campaign to 15-25 accounts routinely gets 20-40%.
**Expensive per account, by design.** Built for a short list worth a large deal.

plan.title: The Share of Model Report
plan.detail: A bound report showing the prospect's real visibility in ChatGPT, Perplexity and Gemini against named competitors. 20 accounts a quarter.

plan.title: The Content Debt Ledger
plan.detail: Their own decaying blog archive presented as financial debt, with a real cost per page. 15 accounts a quarter.

plan.title: The Sealed Competitive Dossier
plan.detail: A confidential-styled analysis of where a named rival is winning in search, Reddit and AI answers. 10-12 accounts a quarter.

plan.title: Coordinated sequences
plan.detail: LinkedIn warm-up before shipping, then heads-up, follow-up and meeting-ask emails timed to delivery.

channels.name: Pipeline
channels.summary: Use AI tools and automation to turn everything above into an attributable pipeline system.
audit: **To be confirmed with the team:** what's already in place (CRM, automation, lead scoring) versus what needs building.

plan.title: Content-to-lead scoring
plan.detail: Track which posts, issues and articles a prospect engages with before a sales conversation.

plan.title: Warm-signal sequences
plan.detail: Repeat engagers get a warmer outreach sequence than a cold list.

plan.title: Intent capture into the CRM
plan.detail: Engagement signals feed whichever CRM the team already uses.

plan.title: A real attribution model
plan.detail: When a deal closes, the content and community touchpoints behind it are logged, not guessed.

prioritiesSub: Every initiative in this plan, placed by expected impact on pipeline against effort to ship. Placement is my estimate from the audit.

contentEngine.weekHint: An illustrative week built from those cadences.

servicesSub: The five things you asked for, grouped into three areas of ownership.

services.title: Executive and social content
services.detail: LinkedIn for Ross and the full leadership team, X, and one repositioned Instagram account.

services.title: Video and community
services.detail: A consistent YouTube engine in two layers, and real volume inside Exit Five.

services.title: Pipeline programs
services.detail: The work that connects content to closed deals, built with the sales team.

roadmapSub: Preceded by a Week 0 discovery sprint with Ross, marketing, content and sales: GTM and sales process, offers and pricing, ICP, competitors, and 6- and 12-month goals. Nothing ships under Foundation's name until that's understood.

roadmap.title: Written content goes live
items: First interviews with all 5-6 executives; pillars set per person
First week of leadership content shipped by Thursday of week 1
X posting live: short-form, threads, articles
Exit Five personas defined, first in-depth content posted
Backend: Instagram and YouTube plan, scripts and TOFU/BOFU split
roadmap.outcome: LinkedIn, X and Exit Five running on cadence; video ready to activate.

roadmap.title: Video goes live
items: Instagram publishing; first YouTube TOFU videos in production
YouTube at the full 4-a-month pace; BOFU format and first guest confirmed
Backend: ABM target accounts and campaign concepts with sales
roadmap.outcome: All five channels live, with an ABM briefing document ready to build.

roadmap.title: ABM and assets ship
items: ABM journey, landing pages and account-specific assets built
Sales and marketing aligned on sequences, signals and handoffs
High-value asset launched with coordinated distribution
roadmap.outcome: First honest attribution report and a specific Q2 recommendation.

outcomesSub: North star: attributed pipeline value connected back to a specific piece of content or community touchpoint. Everything in this plan exists to move that one number.

outcomes.label: Channels live on a repeatable cadence
Closed deal traced back to content

needs: Admin or scheduler access to LinkedIn, X and Instagram
YouTube channel access with upload and edit permissions
CRM access, whichever system is in use
Newsletter and podcast backend access for repurposing
Design support for the magazine, about 1-2 days per issue
Video editing support for Shorts and Reels
A confirmed print partner for the magazine (sourced together in week 1 if needed)
48-hour approvals: drafts in a batch, no response defaults to approved
Trust to operate with an owner's mindset, judged on results

investment.title: Magazine *budget*
investment.sub: Monthly print and postage by volume tier. Design template ($800) is reused each month. Freelance support, AI tooling and a learning budget are scoped in week 1.
investment.note: Recommendation: free for clients and active pipeline. Test a paid option only once engagement is proven.

cta.title: Let's make Foundation *impossible to miss*.
cta.text: A 30-minute call to walk through this plan, pressure-test it against your goals, and agree on what ships first.

footnote: Prepared as a working proposal for Foundation. Figures and timelines are proposed starting points, open to revision once we align. Channel scores and priority placements are estimates from the audit.
